items.title: Conversation vs work-order classifier
items.detail: The brain decides per utterance whether Renne is chatting (answer now) or giving a work order (create a dispatch). Trigger verbs ('dispatch...', 'go do...', 'have the hive...') force a dispatch. This is the front-half of the console — capture + classify.

items.title: Create dispatches in the QI Hive
items.detail: POST :9011/api/dispatch with source='voice_<pc|line|telegram>' and payload {title, description, project, suggested_agent}, landing in the SAME CoWork queue the dashboard already approves. No parallel queue — reuse the verified Hive contract (DB C:\QIH\data\qi_brain.db).

items.title: Approve by voice
items.detail: Say 'approve' / 'go ahead' -> PATCH :9011/api/dispatch/<id> {status:'approved', reviewed_by:'renne'} (or reuse C:\QIH\tools\dispatch_admin.py). Voice becomes the approval surface, keeping inspector findings off the human queue per dispatch-queue-hygiene.

items.title: Net-new dispatch executor
items.detail: A persistent runner polling Brain for approved, source='voice_*' dispatches, executing general work via headless `claude -p` (fanning out to hive-<role> agents) and writing a report to C:\QIH\shared\reports\inbox\. The existing QI_HiveApply pipeline only does allowlisted mechanical fixes — this is the missing general executor.

items.title: Voice notification path
items.detail: There is no push-back today (dispatch status is dashboard-only). Build a watcher: on report/apply-state change, speak / LINE / Telegram 'Done: <result>.' Closes the loop so a spoken order ends in a spoken confirmation.

items.title: Stand up the LiveKit spine
items.detail: Install livekit-server (Windows binary, Apache-2.0, free) and pin a port inside 8720-8729 (NOT 7880 = NEXUS) — register it in qi_registry.json first. One Claude agent serves both the 1:1 voice room (Phase 1) and the multi-party room (Phase 2).

items.title: LiveKit Agent: STT -> brain -> TTS
items.detail: Python agent = faster-whisper distil-large-v3 on CUDA (via RealtimeSTT, ~150-200ms partials) -> the pluggable brain selector -> Kokoro-82M (male am_adam) or edge-tts Andrew, with silero-VAD + smart-turn-v3 endpointing and barge-in. Target ~370-820ms mic->first word.

items.title: Cut over from the CPU loop
items.detail: Upgrade today's CPU base.en Whisper and ~20s/turn realtime.py to the LiveKit agent; retire realtime.py's bespoke loop only after the LiveKit 1:1 voice works (no coverage gap).

items.title: Low-latency live brain
items.detail: Heavy/agentic work stays on the FREE Hive/claude_cli path; add the Anthropic API (Haiku) as a toggleable, disabled-by-default backend purely for snappy conversational replies in live voice.

items.title: LiveKit 'meet' UI
items.detail: Add the simple livekit-examples/meet UI: screen share + chat + recording, with Claude joining as a participant who hears, speaks, and sees shared-screen frames (sampled into Claude's vision).

items.title: plugNmeet full toolkit
items.detail: Upgrade to plugNmeet for document share, whiteboard, breakout rooms, polls — 'most Zoom tools' — once the meet UI is proven.

items.title: Retire the bespoke Meeting Room
items.detail: Replace the hand-rolled WebSocket room (meeting_server.py :8722) with the LiveKit-hosted room once it reaches feature parity, freeing the bespoke STT/TTS/turn-taking code.

items.title: Full backend config panel
items.detail: Extend the :8720 brain UI into the single control surface: backend select + per-backend enable/disable (Ollama + API OFF by default), brain hard-set lock, voice settings — one panel for every surface.

items.title: Speak-in-Claude-Code toggle
items.detail: Objective 4: wire 'voice on' inside a Claude Code session to speak each reply via speak.py (Andrew), with a panel toggle to enable/disable it.

items.title: Delete the dead file bridge
items.detail: Remove claude_bridge/ (bus, bridge_answer, bridge_listen, bridge_speak, inbox/outbox, speak.log) and all _bridge_roundtrip / BRAIN_MODE=='bridge' branches now that the claude_cli backend replaces it. The file bridge needed a human to answer (1 of 12 messages ever answered).

items.title: Retire legacy switches & superseded files
items.detail: Drop the legacy brain_mode single switch and webcall_server.py (superseded by meeting_server.py; both bind :8722).

items.title: Fix the locked live config for realtime
items.detail: Current config is locked->bridge-era with a long bridge_timeout; realtime.py can block per utterance when no session mans the bridge. Cleared by the brain rebuild (now engine=claude_cli) — verify and tidy the timeout.

items.title: Register the QI_ClaudeVoice* services
items.detail: The four NSSM services (Tunnel/Line/Telegram/Control) + two scheduled tasks are installed but not yet recorded in C:\QIH\ecosystem\QI_Service_Registry.md — add them so service triage has a single source of truth.

items.title: Promote the voice bridge as a shared QI feature
items.detail: Package speak.py + listen.py + the realtime loop as a reusable component other QI projects (Maia, OpenClaw 'Koe') can adopt, per the registry's exposes_to_ecosystem entry.

items.title: Boston University replica
items.detail: Keep the dispatch + voice design portable to the BU laptop replica (BU/Implement_Claude_Voice_and_Bridge_at_BU.md): CPU Whisper, loopback-first, secrets in env, no student-data tunneling, same Hive dispatch contract; future SSO/Teams/FERPA hub.

items.title: QI Brain context logging
items.detail: Optionally log Claude Voice sessions/decisions to the QI Brain (:9011) for cross-project memory, as listed in the registry's integrates_with.
